claim: Planarians are capable of whole-body regeneration.
source_text: Planarians are capable of whole-body regeneration and mount distinct molecular responses to wounds that result in tissue absence and those that do not.
evidence_reasoning: This is established scientific knowledge about planarian biology, supported by the citation context of the manuscript.

claim: Planarians mount distinct molecular responses to wounds that result in tissue absence versus wounds that do not result in tissue absence.
source_text: Planarians are capable of whole-body regeneration and mount distinct molecular responses to wounds that result in tissue absence and those that do not.
evidence_reasoning: This represents established findings from prior research that forms the basis for the current study.

claim: Smed-follistatin is required for planarian regeneration.
source_text: We describe a follistatin homolog ( Smed-follistatin ) required for planarian regeneration.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding supported by experimental RNAi data showing regeneration failure in fst(RNAi) animals.

claim: Smed-follistatin inhibition blocks responses to tissue absence but does not prevent normal tissue turnover.
source_text: Smed-follistatin inhibition blocks responses to tissue absence but does not prevent normal tissue turnover.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by experimental observations showing fst(RNAi) animals fail to regenerate but maintain normal tissue homeostasis.

claim: Two activin homologs (Smed-activin-1 and Smed-activin-2) are required for the Smed-follistatin phenotype.
source_text: Two activin homologs ( Smed-activin-1 and Smed-activin-2 ) are required for the Smed-follistatin phenotype.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through genetic suppression experiments showing that activin RNAi rescues the fst(RNAi) phenotype.

claim: Smed-follistatin is wound-induced.
source_text: Finally, Smed-follistatin is wound-induced and expressed at higher levels following injuries that cause tissue absence.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by in situ hybridization data showing fst expression increases at wound sites following amputation.

claim: Smed-follistatin is expressed at higher levels following injuries that cause tissue absence compared to injuries that do not.
source_text: Finally, Smed-follistatin is wound-induced and expressed at higher levels following injuries that cause tissue absence.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated by comparing fst expression levels after tissue wedge removal versus incision injuries.

claim: Smed-follistatin inhibits Smed-Activin proteins to trigger regeneration specifically following injuries involving tissue absence.
source_text: These data suggest that Smed-follistatin inhibits Smed-Activin proteins to trigger regeneration specifically following injuries involving tissue absence and identify a mechanism critical for regeneration initiation, a process important across the animal kingdom.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference from the combined data showing fst requirement, activin suppression of fst phenotype, and differential fst expression based on injury type.

claim: Neoblasts are the only somatic cycling cells in adult planarians.
source_text: Neoblasts are the only somatic cycling cells in adult animals and can be specifically ablated by gamma irradiation, allowing for dissection of the requirements for neoblasts in regenerative processes
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about planarian biology cited from prior research.

claim: Following simple injury, planarians display an increase in mitotic numbers 6 hr after injury before returning to baseline levels.

claim: Animals injected with dsRNA corresponding to non-overlapping sequences from either the 5′ half or the 3′ half of the fst gene failed to regenerate.
source_text: Animals injected with dsRNA corresponding to non-overlapping sequences from either the 5′ half or the 3′ half of the fst gene failed to regenerate (n = 6/14 and 4/16 normal, respectively, compared to 16/16 normal for control)
evidence_reasoning: This is experimental validation data showing the phenotype is specific to fst and not an off-target effect.

claim: fst(RNAi) animals displayed normal anterior sfrp-1 expression 24 hr after amputation but by 8 days displayed none.
source_text: fst(RNAi) animals displayed normal anterior sfrp-1 expression 24 hr after amputation (n = 11/11, top), but by 8 days displayed none (n = 11/12, middle).
evidence_reasoning: This is experimental data showing temporal progression of regeneration failure in fst(RNAi) animals.

claim: fst(RNAi) animals failed to regenerate anterior ndk expression.
source_text: fst(RNAi) animals also failed to regenerate anterior ndk expression (bottom, n = 7/8).
evidence_reasoning: This is experimental data showing failure to regenerate anterior-specific gene expression domains.

claim: fst is expressed at wound sites throughout regeneration, with additional expression in the brain at later timepoints.
source_text: fst is expressed at wound sites throughout regeneration, with additional expression in the brain at later timepoints (arrows, 6 days and 8 days).
evidence_reasoning: This is experimental data from time-course in situ hybridization showing dynamic expression patterns.

claim: Animals were amputated and injected four times with 30 nl fst dsRNA immediately after amputation and a second time 6 hr after amputation, and animals injected with fst dsRNA developed aberrant brains.
source_text: Animals were amputated and injected four times with 30 nl fst dsRNA immediately after amputation and a second time 6 hr after amputation. Animals injected with fst dsRNA developed aberrant brains as labeled by chat expression, and in some cases produced no blastemas (n = 7/10 aberrant, 1/10 no blastema)
evidence_reasoning: This is experimental data showing that post-amputation fst knockdown is sufficient to cause regeneration defects.

claim: Most genes required for regeneration are also required for tissue turnover because of an involvement in neoblast biology.
source_text: Consequently, most genes required for regeneration are also required for tissue turnover because of an involvement in neoblast biology (Reddien et al., 2005).
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about planarian biology cited from prior research.

claim: Unamputated fst(RNAi) animals did not shrink or lose structures, as is typically seen in animals with neoblast dysfunction, even after several months of significant expression reduction with RNAi.
source_text: Strikingly, unamputated fst(RNAi) animals did not shrink or lose structures, as is typically seen in animals with neoblast dysfunction, even after several months of significant expression reduction with RNAi (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence_reasoning: This is experimental observation data showing the unusual specificity of the fst phenotype.

claim: Amputated fst(RNAi) animals—despite failing to regenerate—displayed ongoing long-term neoblast-based tissue turnover of remaining tissue.
source_text: Furthermore, amputated animals—despite failing to regenerate—displayed ongoing long-term neoblast-based tissue turnover of remaining tissue (Figure 1D).
evidence_reasoning: This is experimental data showing dissociation between regeneration and homeostatic tissue maintenance.

claim: New tissues are formed at planarian wound sites in a process called blastema formation.
source_text: New tissues are formed at planarian wound sites in a process called blastema formation, and pre-existing tissues are reorganized after amputation to accommodate reduced animal size and further generate missing tissues
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about planarian regeneration biology.

claim: Pre-existing tissues are reorganized after amputation to accommodate reduced animal size and further generate missing tissues.
source_text: New tissues are formed at planarian wound sites in a process called blastema formation, and pre-existing tissues are reorganized after amputation to accommodate reduced animal size and further generate missing tissues (Morgan, 1901; Reddien and Sánchez Alvarado, 2004).
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about morphallaxis in planarians.

claim: The source of regenerated tissue in planarians is a population of adult dividing cells called neoblasts.
source_text: The source of regenerated tissue in planarians is a population of adult dividing cells called neoblasts (Reddien and Sánchez Alvarado, 2004), which include pluripotent stem cells called clonogenic neoblasts (cNeoblasts) (Wagner et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about the cellular basis of planarian regeneration.

claim: Neoblasts include pluripotent stem cells called clonogenic neoblasts (cNeoblasts).
source_text: The source of regenerated tissue in planarians is a population of adult dividing cells called neoblasts (Reddien and Sánchez Alvarado, 2004), which include pluripotent stem cells called clonogenic neoblasts (cNeoblasts) (Wagner et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about neoblast heterogeneity cited from prior research.

claim: Head amputation normally induces neoblasts to produce ovo+ eye progenitors.
source_text: Head amputation normally induces neoblasts to produce ovo+ eye progenitors (Lapan and Reddien, 2012), but this process failed in fst(RNAi) animals
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from prior research establishing normal progenitor production dynamics.

claim: wntP-2 is normally expressed in planarian tails and its expression domain restricts posteriorly within 48 hr of amputation whether regeneration proceeds or not.
source_text: For example, wntP-2 (also known as wnt11-5 [Gurley et al., 2010]) is normally expressed in planarian tails (Petersen and Reddien, 2009; Gurley et al., 2010) and its expression domain restricts posteriorly within 48 hr of amputation whether regeneration proceeds or not (Gurley et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from prior research establishing normal morphallaxis dynamics.

claim: Smed-delta-1 displays higher expression after an incision or puncture (simple injuries) than after amputation (a major injury).
source_text: Notably, some wound-induced genes display expression that inversely scales with missing tissue amount; for example, Smed-delta-1 displays higher expression after an incision or puncture (simple injuries) than after amputation (a major injury) (Wenemoser et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from prior research characterizing wound-induced gene expression patterns.

claim: Irradiated animals (which cannot regenerate) can display either higher or lower levels of wound-induced expression, depending on the gene examined.
source_text: Irradiated animals (which cannot regenerate) can display either higher or lower levels of wound-induced expression, depending on the gene examined (Wenemoser et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from prior research characterizing wound responses in irradiated animals.

claim: The missing-tissue gene expression defects of fst(RNAi) animals cannot be explained as a side-effect of regenerative failure.
source_text: As was the case for the failed apoptotic response of fst(RNAi) animals, the missing-tissue gene expression defects of fst(RNAi) animals cannot therefore be explained as a side-effect of regenerative failure.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference from comparing fst(RNAi) phenotypes with irradiated animals and other regeneration-defective conditions.

claim: Following head amputation, head fragments not only produce posterior-specific cell types but also reduce numbers of anterior-specific cell types (which are overabundant for the new fragment dimensions).
source_text: Following head amputation, head fragments not only produce posterior-specific cell types but also reduce numbers of anterior-specific cell types (which are overabundant for the new fragment dimensions).
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about morphallaxis processes in planarian regeneration.

claim: RNAi of smad1 blocked blastema formation but did not block pharynx formation.
source_text: By contrast, RNAi of a different gene that blocked blastema formation (smad1) did not block pharynx formation, indicating this defect is not a simple consequence of blastema formation failure
evidence_reasoning: This is experimental data providing a control comparison to demonstrate specificity of the fst phenotype.

claim: The pharynx formation defect in fst(RNAi) animals is not a simple consequence of blastema formation failure.
source_text: By contrast, RNAi of a different gene that blocked blastema formation (smad1) did not block pharynx formation, indicating this defect is not a simple consequence of blastema formation failure (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference from the comparison between fst(RNAi) and smad1(RNAi) phenotypes.

claim: Persistence of wound-induced gene expression is an aspect of the planarian missing-tissue response.
source_text: In addition to the cellular responses to missing tissue described above, persistence of wound-induced gene expression is another aspect of the planarian missing-tissue response (Wenemoser et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This is cited from prior research characterizing the missing-tissue response.
